findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes reminders of any method and any scheduled state
findings.body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not constrained by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` or `scheduled: false`. Because `retryCount` lives on the shared `WorkflowReminder` model, this SMS cron can delete email/WhatsApp reminders, and can also delete a reminder whose SMS has already been scheduled if its retry count ever exceeds 1 (for example through interleaved cron runs). Those rows are then permanently lost, so later cancellation logic cannot find the scheduled reminder. Scope the retry branch to SMS unscheduled reminders, e.g. `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

findings.title: Retry count uses a stale read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment
findings.body: Both failure paths write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched once before the loop. If two cron invocations overlap—there is no locking in this endpoint—or the row is updated by another process, one increment is lost, so the reminder can be retried more times than intended and deletion is delayed or skipped. Use an atomic Prisma update such as `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` (ideally with a claim/conditional update so overlapping runs do not both send).

findings.title: Every exception is treated as an SMS send failure and consumes the retry budget
findings.body: The catch wraps the whole per-reminder flow, not just `twilio.scheduleSMS`. Errors from profile lookup, URL generation, template rendering, or the DB update after Twilio has already accepted the SMS all increment `retryCount`. After two such errors the reminder is deleted. This means transient failures such as a database hiccup or Twilio outage can permanently drop reminders, and a DB update failure after a successful Twilio schedule leaves the row unscheduled so the next run can schedule a duplicate SMS. Only increment for confirmed send failures, and handle post-send persistence errors separately.

findings.title: Retry update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` inside `catch` is not itself guarded. If it fails—for example because another cron invocation deleted the row, or the database is unavailable—the error escapes the catch and aborts the handler loop. The remaining unscheduled reminders are then not processed and the endpoint returns an error. The retry bookkeeping should not be able to stop the batch; catch and log failures around it (or use an updateMany and continue).

findings.title: No tests cover the new retry/deletion behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a schema column, retry increments on two failure paths, and deletion after the retry limit, but no tests were added. There is no coverage proving that a reminder is kept after one failure, deleted after two failures, that successful scheduling does not get deleted, or that non-SMS reminders are not removed by this SMS cron. These are exactly the failure-sensitive branches where regressions are likely.
